text:
IncidentBot: P1 page to #incidents: High error rate for NorthStar Finance (Private VPC / Dedicated pool). API 502s and timeouts observed since 07:12 UTC. Customers seeing failed model calls. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

Sara W: I'm taking this. I see an alert spike in the Dedicated pool for region-us-east-2. Symptoms: 502s on /v1/generate, connection resets, and intermittent DNS NXDOMAIN for customer model hostnames.

NorthStar Oncall: Confirmed: production is degraded, we see ~40% request failures; some requests time out before response. Impacting end users.

Sara W: Thanks. Quick triage plan: 1) check NLB target health, 2) verify security groups and ALB (if present), 3) confirm customer's DNS answers, 4) look for conntrack / ephemeral port exhaustion.

Mike K: Noted. I'll pull NLB target group status (us-east-2 / nlb-id-abc). Run: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...`

Anita R: Also check VPC Flow Logs for REJECT from customer subnet to our egress. Ran a quick query: seeing a flurry of RSTs to our egress IPs around 07:11-07:14 UTC.

Mike K: Target health shows 2/6 healthy, some targets Unhealthy -> reason: TLS handshake timeout / connection refused.

Sara W: Can the customer confirm if they changed any firewall / security group rules?

NorthStar Oncall: We rolled out an egress SG change at ~07:05 to restrict outbound to a smaller CIDR. Reverting now and will confirm in 2 minutes.

Ryan (on-call): If they narrowed egress, that could break NLB health checks or upstream model host connections. Check security groups for ephemeral ports (1024-65535) and outbound DNS (UDP/53).

Sara W: Running quick checks: `dig +short model-ns.northstar.private` from a host in the dedicated pool returns nothing intermittently. Locally able to replicate NXDOMAIN from some AZs.

Mike K: Also seeing high connection attempt rate to customer firewall -> many SYNs, few ACKs. Suggest restoring customer outbound rules. If they can't, we can put an ALB in front of the pool in a different subnet as temporary workaround.

NorthStar Oncall: Reverted the SG change at 07:18. I see DNS returning again from our side, can you confirm?

Anita R: After revert, NLB target health improved for 4 of 6 targets, still 2 failing with TLS handshake timeouts. Could be backend process stuck.

Sara W: Ok next steps: a) force-restart the two unhealthy targets (graceful restart), b) clear conntrack on the nodes if NAT/conntrack exhaustion suspected, c) keep DNS retries / caching short to observe.

Mike K: Restarted worker on ip-10-1-9-21 (unhealthy). `systemctl restart inference-worker` executed at 07:25 UTC. Watching logs.

Anita R: Running `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` shows high counts on nodes; on one NAT instance count ~ 95k (threshold ~100k). Still under but trending up. We'll tail /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count.

Ryan (on-call): If conntrack is creeping, reduce connection churn: enable keepalives or increase NAT table, and in the short term re-register targets across different ENIs to spread connections.

Sara W: Applied temporary increase: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` on NAT instances at 07:31 UTC. Also toggled keepalive to 60s.

Mike K: After worker restart and conntrack bump, two previously unhealthy targets are now healthy. NLB target health 6/6 at 07:36 UTC.

NorthStar Oncall: From our side traffic is recovering. We still saw about 4 minutes of customer-visible errors. Any residual actions we should take?

Sara W: For immediate mitigation, customers get degraded for ~07:12-07:36. We: reworked SG, restarted workers, increased conntrack, rebalanced targets. As a fallback we also prepared a route to fail traffic to Hosted pool (redwood-hosted fallback) but didn't cut over.

Anita R: Observed a related DNS TTL caching behavior — some worker hosts cached NXDOMAIN for 300s. We'll add a post-incident step to reduce negative caching and add retry jitter.

Mike K: Also saw few TLS handshake failures tied to a flaky node disk IO (high iowait). We queued disk maintenance for that host (EBS check + instance reprovision).

Ryan (on-call): Customer isolation notes: this was a customer-side SG change that had cascade effects due to our health checks and NAT conntrack interaction. No other tenants impacted. Confirmed Dedicated pool scoped to NorthStar.

Sara W: I'll open an incident ticket with timeline and customer impact: start 07:12 UTC, mitigation completed 07:36 UTC, customer reported revert 07:18 UTC, final healthy 07:36 UTC. Severity P1. Estimated user impact: ~4 minutes of elevated errors, partial degradations until targets recovered.

NorthStar Oncall: Thanks — we'll review internal change process for SG updates and work with your SREs to coordinate out-of-band changes next time.

Anita R: Immediate action items (assigned): \n- Anita: run EBS health and reprovision ip-10-1-9-21 (done in maintenance window)\n- Mike: add health-check jitter and reduce negative NXDOMAIN TTLs in host resolver (follow-up PR)\n- Sara: post-incident customer communication draft + timeline\n- Ryan: review NAT conntrack thresholds and implement alert at 80%

Sara W: Adding a runbook note: when customer VPC egress rules change, expect NLB target flapping + DNS NXDOMAIN ripples. Steps: check customer SG rules, run `dig` from within pool, check `aws elbv2 describe-target-health`, examine conntrack and nat metrics, restart unhealthy workers, consider temporary conntrack bump, and notify customer to revert.

Mike K: Link to quick commands in thread: 
```
# from worker node
dig @169.254.169.253 model-ns.northstar.private
curl -v --resolve model-ns.northstar.private:443:<nlb-ip> https://model-ns.northstar.private/health
sudo conntrack -L | tail -n 50
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn>
```

Anita R: I'll draft the RCA skeleton and schedule a postmortem with NorthStar and infra.

Sara W: Closing notes: no SLA credit expected (short duration), but flagging for customer ops review. Great cross-team work to get targets healthy quickly. :thumbsup:

Ryan (on-call): Will follow up with a test to simulate SG narrowings in staging to catch this earlier.

Mike K: Marking thread resolved for now — monitoring for 24h.

IncidentBot: Incident P1 ticket #INC-2026 created and linked to this thread.
